intro: Switzerland is a federal republic famous for direct democracy: citizens vote on national issues several times a year.

chapters.title: Direct democracy
text: Any law passed by parliament can be challenged in a referendum if 50,000 people sign a petition, and 100,000 signatures can force a national vote on a change to the constitution. In two small cantons, citizens still vote by raising their hands in an open-air assembly.

chapters.title: Seven leaders
text: Switzerland has no single head of state. A Federal Council of seven ministers leads the country together, and one of them serves as president for just one year. The parliament has a National Council and a Council of States.

The red square flag with a white cross is one of only two square national flags, with the Vatican's. Geneva hosts many UN agencies and the Red Cross, Lausanne the International Olympic Committee and Zürich FIFA.
